answer: Every identity must tie to a river’s sediment profile logged by a pigment-sensitive stilt-sensor array. Sybils must replicate the gradient, burning 0.05 grams of raw pigment per head since bulk farms degrade the stilt’s prism optics. Misalignment costs 12 milliseconds of recalibration time, a cost that compounds because overlapping calibrations collapse riverbank contours into unreadable noise.
